payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_session.py::test_the_generic_stub_answers_spec_ids_without_a_real_grep_call stayed green with the criterion's own edit applied to saffron/cell/worktree.py. The claim was '`_stub_the_runtime` (tests/test_session.py:1180) stubs `saffron.cell.worktree.dirty_paths` to an empty-list lambda right beside its other worktree stubs (tests/test_session.py:1379), but stubs no such thing for the sibling `saffron.cell.worktree.spec_ids` that `GateSuite._run` also reads off every `Tree` it is handed (saffron/gates/suite.py). Left unstubbed, a call to `spec_ids` falls through to the fixture\'s own catch-all `saffron.cell.runtime.exec_` double (tests/test_session.py:1281), which logs the real `git grep` argv into `cell.execs` and returns it empty. Add `monkeypatch.setattr("saffron.cell.worktree.spec_ids", lambda container: [])` immediately after the `dirty_paths` line, the same shape as its sibling. The witness drives one ordinary two-turn cell through `_stub_the_runtime` and `_drive`, reaching `READY_FOR_REVIEW`, where `GateSuite.baseline` and `GateSuite.against` both read `tree.spec_ids()` on the implementer cell (`saffron-cell-SY-1`). It asserts that no entry in `cell.execs` is the id-listing `git grep` argv, which only holds once the stub is in place.'. Under the edit the whole `tests` gate failed tests/test_session.py::test_the_lens_gate_cell_holds_no_credential_and_is_gone_before_any_lens_runs, tests/test_worktree.py::test_the_suite_judges_cited_ids_against_the_spec_files_at_head, and the criterion's witness did not fail.
